hypothesis: Below 10 GiB of --vram the HIP placement keeps the shared experts in RAM, the condition V4_HOT_SPLIT needs. Turning the split on there by itself (V4_HOT_SPLIT unset) makes decode faster than the plain GPU tier at every --vram the 8 GB card takes, with the same text.
model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash architecture, REAP-pruned to 132 experts x 43 layers (79 GB), safetensors, native FP8/FP4
command: make -C c -j16 deepseek-v4 HIP=1 HIP_ARCH=gfx1102 ROCM_HOME=/usr (hipcc's default 32-lane waves); deepseek_v4 <model> 'Count from 1 to 300, separated by single spaces.' --max-tokens 200 with the environment in config (--vram N as CUDA_EXPERT_GB=N); one binary; the arms alternate (trial, baseline) three times at --vram 4, then at 6; tok_s = (generated - 1) / after_first from the engine's `timing` line (decode throughput). Also on that binary: vram5_trial (one run), vram6_* (three runs per arm), vram7_trial (three runs; the plain tier does not fit beside the desktop at --vram 7: it peaks about 180 MiB above --vram), cpu_reference (COLI_CUDA=0, three runs)
